target_customer: First responders, law enforcement and military units that need to detect people behind walls
problem: Existing through-wall detection devices were heavy and cumbersome. Lumineye built portable tactical radar sensors that detect and track people through walls.
business_model: Hardware sales to government and public safety customers, plus government grants and prizes

founders.name: Megan Lacy
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page: CEO for several years, then board role in August 2023; elite runner.

founders.name: Corbin Hennen
founders.background_notes: Named by TechCrunch and the YC page, no background given.

founders.name: Robert Kleffner
founders.background_notes: Named by TechCrunch and the YC page; described there as a programming enthusiast.

exit.reason: Cause not public. YC lists the company as Inactive.

competitors.name: Camero-Tech Xaver
competitors.what: Israeli sense through wall radar line from handheld Xaver 100 to 3D Xaver 800 for tactical forces
competitors.traction_then: Products sold to military and police for years; the Xaver 800 won a 2007 officer.com innovation award

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a portable radar that detects breathing through walls requires RF hardware design, signal processing and field ruggedization, hard for a ten person team.

defensibility.rationale: Radar design expertise and government certification pathways raise the barrier, but Camero and L3 products already existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying or buying Lumineye; the company went inactive for undisclosed reasons.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in August 2019 said existing detection machines were heavy and cumbersome, and the Army ran an xTechSearch competition in 2019 that Lumineye won, showing government demand for the capability.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline X-ray Vision for First Responders

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch, Army Times and defense press in 2019.

brand_strength.rationale: A clear tagline and some defense press, but no consumer brand assets and the name's origin and identity were not documented.

outcome_analysis: Lumineye built portable through-wall radar after the Stanford Hacking for Defense program, joined YC in Summer 2019 and won an Army xTechSearch prize in October 2019. It is now Inactive and no post mortem or acquisition report was found, so the cause of the stall is not public.
notes: The $250,000 xTechSearch figure rests on a search snippet of the Army and SOFREP coverage and I did not open the article to confirm amount or exact month; treat date 2019-10 as approximate (Army Times piece dated 2019-10-24). SBIR awards exist (a Phase II listed at $799,842 on an Air Force topic) but I did not open the pages, so they are not recorded as rounds. Crunchbase and Dealroom pages gave no figures. Competitor Range-R from L3 omitted because the only source found is undated. Founder education not found.
